text: Welcome to the clinic. I am Dr. Agent; I see you are a neonate presenting with seizures and lethargy three days after birth. To understand the cause, I must ask: Have you noticed any jaundice, poor feeding, or fever, and has anyone seen any unusual skin rashes or discoloration?

speaker: Patient
text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor

text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Intraventricular Hemorrhage (Grade II or III), likely secondary to perinatal asphyxia and chorioamnionitis in a preterm infant.

The clinical picture of seizures, lethargy, low birth weight, and a history of chorioamnionitis, combined with the ultrasound finding of intraventricular bleeding, strongly supports this diagnosis. The pending metabolic and coagulation results will help rule out sepsis or bleeding disorders, but the hemorrhage is the immediate cause of the neurological symptoms.
